name: Denoising Autoencoder
analogy: Think of it as a restorer who practises on deliberately damaged paintings. A clean chart-pattern is smudged on purpose, the restorer must repaint the original, and over thousands of tries learns what a normal picture is supposed to look like. A canvas that cannot be restored to anything normal stands out.

steps.title: Take a clean window of market features
steps.description: Each training example is a short stretch of bars described by a set of numbers, such as returns, range and volume measures, all rescaled so no single number dominates. The clean version is kept aside as the answer key.
steps.inExample: A window of 30 five-minute MNQ bars, each described by 6 rescaled features, gives 180 clean numbers.

steps.title: Damage it on purpose
steps.description: A copy of the window is corrupted: some numbers are blanked out, or small random noise is added, or both. The strength of the damage is a setting. Too little and the task is trivial; too much and nothing can be recovered.
steps.inExample: 20 percent of the 180 numbers are blanked and a small amount of random noise is added to the rest.

steps.title: Squeeze the damaged window into a short code
steps.description: The encoder reads the damaged window and compresses it into a much shorter list of numbers, the code. Because the code is short, the network cannot memorise; it has to keep only the structure that matters.
steps.inExample: The 180 damaged numbers are compressed to a code of 16 numbers.

steps.title: Rebuild the clean window from the code
steps.description: The decoder expands the code back into a full window. The network is rewarded when the rebuilt window matches the original clean one, not the damaged one it was shown.
steps.inExample: The decoder outputs 180 numbers; the average gap from the original clean window is about 9 percent of a typical feature's spread.

steps.title: Repeat on many windows until repairs are good
steps.description: Steps one to four repeat over a long history of windows. The network adjusts so that typical market structure is repaired well. It learns what normal windows share, such as how range and volume usually move together.
steps.inExample: After training on about 400,000 windows, typical windows are rebuilt with an average gap near 9 percent of a feature's spread.

steps.title: Use the code, or the repair error, afterwards
steps.description: On new data, the short code serves as a cleaned-up summary to feed another model. The rebuild error is also useful: a window the network cannot repair well is unusual compared with what it has seen.
steps.inExample: Today's window rebuilds with an error of 18 percent, twice the typical 9 percent, so it is flagged as unusual.

useFor.example: Turning 30 bars of 6 features into a code of 16 numbers to feed a tree model or classifier.
Raising a warning when a window's rebuild error is above its 99th percentile, as around a surprise economic release.
Filling in a few missing or glitched volume readings in a window using the structure learned from normal data.
Learning a representation of years of unlabelled MNQ and ES bars before any direction labels are applied.

avoidWhen: You need a direct buy-or-sell probability; a model trained on direction labels answers that question directly, and the code only helps indirectly.
Your features are mostly random noise to begin with; the network will faithfully learn to repair noise and the code will carry nothing useful.

example.scenario: A researcher wants to know whether the current MNQ window is ordinary or unusual. A denoising autoencoder trained on a year of 5-minute windows is shown the latest 30 bars, and returns a short code and how well it could repair the window.

input.summary: One window of 30 five-minute bars described by 6 rescaled features, optionally with some values blanked.

fields.name: window length
fields.meaning: The number of bars in the window being summarised.

fields.name: features per bar
fields.meaning: Return, range, body share, wick balance, volume and trade count, all rescaled.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The recent typical bar travel, which is high for a calm morning.

fields.name: volume against its 20-bar average
fields.meaning: A heavy-volume window, unusual for this time of day.

fields.name: share of numbers blanked at test time
fields.meaning: At scoring time the window is given clean, with no damage added.

output.summary: A short code for the window and the error of the rebuilt window against the original.

fields.name: code
fields.meaning: The compressed summary of the window that other models can use as input.

fields.name: rebuild error
fields.meaning: The average gap between the rebuilt and the original window, as a share of a typical feature's spread.

fields.name: typical rebuild error in training
fields.meaning: The average gap for ordinary windows, used as the comparison.

fields.name: percentile of this error
fields.meaning: Where today's error ranks among all training windows; higher means more unusual.

example.reading: An error twice the typical one, in the top 1 percent, says this window is unlike most of what the model has seen. That is a reason to look at the chart and reduce size, not a forecast of direction. If you use the 16-number code downstream, test it against the raw features to see that it adds something.
